statements.t: • As announced on September 30, 2026, construction is underway on AGE’s 70 MW biomass cogeneration project, in which we hold a 14% equity interest.
The resulting reduction in projected cash flows led to the recognition of $212 million in non-cash impairments of our Temiscaming plant assets.

In March 2026, a grant agreement was signed with the European Climate, Infrastructure and Environmental Executive Agency that positions Verso’s ReSTart project (Renewable e-SAF Tartas) to become one of the first large-scale synthetic aviation fuel production plants in Europe through the capture of biogenic CO 2 emissions from our Tartas HPC plant.
We are targeting a conclusion of the strategic review in Q1 2027.
We expect CS volumes to exit 2026 at or near a run rate of 100,000 MT per quarter, consistent with previous expectations.
Our second-half earnings outlook remains unchanged.
We will continue to maintain disciplined control of discretionary spending and pursue structural efficiencies across the organization.

We will continue to prioritize capital expenditures for essential maintenance and reliability, along with initiatives that support near-term cash generation and offer attractive risk-adjusted returns.

Through year end, we will continue to actively manage working capital, capital spending and operating costs, including Temiscaming’s ongoing carrying costs, with a focus on maintaining appropriate liquidity and compliance with our debt covenants.

We believe our future cash flows from operations, availability under our ABL Credit Facility and our ability to access the capital markets, if necessary or desirable, will be adequate to fund our operations and anticipated long-term funding requirements, including capital expenditures, defined benefit plan contributions and repayment of debt maturities.

The declaration and payment of future common stock dividends, if any, will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and dependent upon our financial condition, results of operations, capital requirements and other factors that the Board of Directors deems relevant.
We have not repurchased shares under this program since 2018 and do not expect to utilize any of the remaining $60 million in unused authorization in the future.
These measures are not defined by GAAP and our discussion of them is not intended to conflict with or change any of our GAAP disclosures provided in this report.
• Strategic review continues with interested parties; tariff-related uncertainty at Temiscaming has slowed the process and we are now targeting a conclusion in Q1 2027
We also see opportunities to create long-term value by leveraging our existing infrastructure, including through the Altamaha Green Energy project at Jesup, where construction is underway.
Given the complexities of these discussions, we are targeting a conclusion of the strategic review in Q1 2027.”
A replay of this webcast will be archived on the Company’s website shortly after the call.

As a result, all financial results described in this earnings release should be considered preliminary and are subject to change to reflect any necessary adjustments or changes in accounting estimates that are identified prior to the time the Company files its Form 10-Q.

Financial Risks The Company may need to make significant additional cash contributions to its retirement benefit plans if investment returns on pension assets are lower than expected or interest rates decline, and/or due to changes to regulatory, accounting and actuarial requirements.
